title: A protocol for live imaging of pancreatic tissue
protocol: Anesthetize mouse with a mixture of ketamine/xylazine (100/10 mg/kg, intraperitoneal injection).
Wait until the mouse has an unresponsive pedal reflex (toe pinch) before proceeding.
Continue to perform toe pinch at regular intervals throughout the procedure to monitor depth of anesthesia.
Administer 0.5 ml PBS by IP injection every two hours during the protocol to keep the animal hydrated.
Maintain the animal on a heating pad set at 37°C.
Apply ophthalmic ointment to eyes using a cotton applicator to prevent drying during the procedure.
Inject fluorescent dyes or fluorescently-conjugated antibodies intravenously (retro-orbital or tail vein injection).
Use Hoescht 33342 to visualize nuclei (10 μl of a 20 mM stock solution per mouse).
Use VE-cadherin antibodies conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 to visualize the vasculature (50 μg in 100 μl per mouse).
Position the mouse lateral side up.
Thoroughly spray the abdomen and back with 70% ethanol.
Locate the most distal rib.

Make an incision approximately 0.5 cm below the final rib extending 2 cm toward the ventral side of the body and 2 cm toward the distal side, ensuring penetration through skin and body wall but avoiding injury to the spleen.
Turn on isoflurane regulator at a rate of 1-3% isoflurane in oxygen.
Position mouse with the incision facing up on the imaging apparatus connected to the anesthesia system.
Carefully lift the tail of the pancreas and the spleen through the incision onto the surface of the imaging apparatus using sterile blunt forceps.
Secure the tissue to the imaging apparatus by placing a coverslip over the tail of the pancreas.
Keep the pancreas hydrated by supplying PBS between the coverslip and imaging apparatus.
Transfer the imaging apparatus to the microscope.
Perform imaging using a TCS SP5 upright DM600 CFS Leica confocal system and Leica LAS AF 2.7.3 software.
Acquire images using an HCX APO L20x objective with a 1.0 numerical aperture.
Place 2-3 drops of distilled water on the coverslip before lowering the objective if the objective requires water immersion.
Excite the fluorophore of interest using the appropriate laser.
Use the Argon-ion (458 nm and 488 nm) and Diode pumped solid-state (561 nm) lasers to excite Hoescht 33342, GFP, and DsRed2 respectively.
Image approximately 100 microns deep into the pancreas using this system.
Euthanize the mouse by cervical dislocation after completing the imaging session.
Anesthetize mouse with a mixture of ketamine/xylazine (100/10 mg/kg, intraperitoneal injection).
Wait until mouse has an unresponsive pedal reflex (toe pinch) to proceed.
Administer the desired fluorescent dyes or fluorescently-conjugated antibodies intravenously (retro-orbital or tail vein injection).
Inject Hoescht 33342 for nuclear visualization at a dose of 10 μl of a 20 mM stock solution per mouse.
Inject VE-cadherin antibodies conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 for vasculature visualization (50 μg in 100 μl per mouse).
If dyes are injected retro-orbitally, limit the volume to a maximum of 100 μl per eye (a total of 200 μl in both eyes).
Position the mouse ventral side up.
Thoroughly spray the abdomen with 70% ethanol.
Use sterile forceps and surgical scissors to make two incisions from the center of the abdomen to the lateral and medial side of the rib cage.
Remove the tumor using forceps and scissors.
Place the removed tumor in a 60 cm culture dish.
Rest a coverslip on the tumor.
Stabilize the coverslip against the edge of the culture dish.
